children.text: abhinavā nūtanā bhānavīyā bhānavaḥ sāvitrā raśmayo vo yuṣmabhyaṃ vibhūtyai samṛddhyai bhūyāsurbhavantu ||
children.translated_text: May the fresh, new, solar rays, the rays belonging to <s>Savitṛ</s>, become for you vibhūti (prosperous power), that is, abundance.
Doing what?

children.text: sindūrareṇuśca sāndro bahalaḥ sindūrareṇuḥ sindūrarajastaddadhata iva ||
children.translated_text: As if bearing dense vermilion dust, namely thick vermilion powder, red pigment.
Of what kind?

children.text: jambhasyārātirjambhārātiḥ śakrastasyebho hastī airāvaṇastasya kumbhau mastakau tayostau vā udbhavo yasyeti vigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Jambhārāti</s>' means the enemy of <s>Jambha</s>, <s>Śakra</s>; his elephant is <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, and its kumbhas are the two frontal globes of its head. The analysis is: that from which those two arise, or that which has them as its source.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati ye svargasthāste udayarāgabhṛtas tān avalokyairāvaṇakumbhasthaṃ sindūrareṇuṃ dadhata iva manyante ||
children.translated_text: This is what is meant: those who are in heaven, seeing them bearing the redness of dawn, think that they are as if carrying the vermilion dust from <s>Airāvaṇa</s>'s frontal globes.

children.text: udayaścāsau giriśca tasya taṭī tasyā dhātavo gairikādayasteṣāṃ dhārākāro dravo dhārādravaḥ prapātastasyevaughaiḥ pravāhaiḥ samūhairavicchinnaiḥ siktā ata eva raktā iva ||
children.translated_text: The dawn-mountain, and its slope; the minerals on it, such as red ochre; the stream-like liquid of those minerals, a cascade; by its torrents, streams, and continuous masses they seem sprinkled and therefore red.

children.text: udayagiristhānām evaṃ buddhirjāyate tulyakālaṃ samakālam āyāntyā āgacchantyā padmakhaṇḍadīptyā ivāruṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those situated on the dawn-mountain this understanding arises: they are red as if from the radiance of a mass of lotuses arriving at the same time.
Together with <s>Savitṛ</s> himself the glow of the lotus-groves arrives.
In this way, through the radiance, the perception arises for those on the earth.
What are the rays doing?
They are illuminating the three worlds.
Their freshness is with reference to their making the directions visible.

children.text: te bhāskarasya karā vo yuṣmākaṃ kalyāṇaṃ kriyāsur vidheyāsuḥ ||
children.translated_text: May those hands, that is rays, of <s>Bhāskara</s> perform welfare for you.
They cause the opening of lotus-groves; they bring about the unfolding of clusters of lotuses.
He imagines them as if wishing to draw out <s>Lakṣmī</s>, as if their minds were set on pulling her forth.
Because it is as though they wish to draw out <s>Lakṣmī</s>, who is always present in lotus-groves.
For what purpose?
To give her, to bestow her.
To whom?
To one bowed down by devotion.
One bent low through devotion is 'devotion-bowed'; to him.
What sort of prosperity?
One lying hidden in the hollow interior of the hut formed by the cup of a bud.
By the word 'bud' a closed blossom is meant.

children.text: tasya yaḥ puṭaḥ sa eva kuṭī śāleva mukulapuṭakuṭī tasyāḥ koṭaramabhyantaraṃ tasya kroḍo'vanamrapradeśastatra līnāṃ saṃśliṣṭām ||
children.translated_text: Its cup is itself a hut, like a little chamber; the hollow of that bud-cup-hut is its interior, and the lap is the downward-bending place there. She is lying there, clinging within it.
What kind of rays?
Able to destroy the fear of the world that has fallen into the mouth of darkness shaped like <s>Kāla</s>.

children.text: kālasyevākāro yasya sa kālākāraḥ sa cāsāvandhakāraśca tasyānanaṃ mukhaṃ tatra patitaṃ yajjagattasya sādhvasaṃ bhayaṃ tasya dhvaṃso nāśastatra kalyāḥ paṭavaḥ samarthā eva ||
children.translated_text: That whose form is like <s>Kāla</s> is 'Kāla-shaped'; and that is darkness. Into its mouth has fallen the world; they are capable, indeed competent, in destroying the fear of that world.
Again, what are their characteristics?
They have the sheen of tender shoots; their lustre is like that of new sprouts.
May the feet of <s>Bradhna</s>, the sun, that is his rays, protect and guard.
Whom?
You.
Doing what?

children.text: ambhoruhāṇāṃ padmānāṃ garbheṣvabhyantareṣu śikhariṣu ca parvateṣu śitāgreṣu tīkṣṇaprānteṣu tulyaṃ samaṃ patanto gacchantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Falling, that is proceeding, equally into the interiors of lotuses and onto mountains, onto sharp peaks with pointed ends.

children.text: anyasya hi pādā yathā haritaśādvalopacitāyāṃ bhūmau nipatanti tathā na śarkarilāyāṃ kaṇṭakitāyāṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: For another person's feet fall on ground covered with green grass, but not in the same way on gravelly or thorny ground.

children.text: bradhnasya punarmārdavātiśayayukteṣu padmagarbheṣu tīkṣṇaśṛṅgeṣu ca parvateṣu samaṃ patanti ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Bradhna</s>'s feet fall equally on the very soft interiors of lotuses and on mountains with sharp peaks.

children.text: vāsarasya divasasya prārambhe mukhe tasyaiva vyuparatisamaye cāstamanakāle tathaiva sadṛśā ekarūpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning, the face of the day, and likewise at its cessation, at sunset, they are similar, of one form.

children.text: tribhuvanaṃ bhavanaprāṅgaṇamiva tribhuvanabhavanaprāṅgaṇaṃ tasmiṃstrailokyaveśmājire niṣparyāyamavidyamānakramaṃ pravṛttāḥ prasṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They move forth without succession, without any interval, in the courtyard of the mansion of the three worlds, as if the three worlds were a house-courtyard.

children.text: anyasya hi pādāścaraṇā gṛhāṅgaṇe paryāyeṇa pravartante ||
children.translated_text: For another person's feet, his steps, move in a house-courtyard one after another.
His, however, move all at the same time.
Bearing heat, warmth, intensely; possessing it exceedingly.
He imagines it as if born from the fatigue of constant travel.
That which is continuous and is also a road is a continuous road.
Here the word 'road' is used in the sense of excessive going.
Fatigue comes from that; as if it were born from that fatigue.
Intensely, uninterruptedly, densely: as if produced by weariness from movement.

children.text: anyo hi yaḥ pānthastasya pādā ūṣmāṇameva bibhrati dadhati ||
children.translated_text: For any other traveller's feet bear heat in just this way.

children.text: te raśmayo marīcayo maṅgalaṃ kalyāṇaṃ vo diśantu dadatu ||
children.translated_text: May those rays, the beams, grant and give you auspicious welfare.

children.text: yān kiraṇāṃstigmarocis tīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ sūryo vitanute vistārayati ||
children.translated_text: Those rays which the sharp-rayed sun, <s>Tigmarocis</s>, spreads and extends.
In what manner?
So that it becomes broad and extensive.
Having done what?

children.text: jantūnprāṇino vītāvṛtīn āvaraṇamāvṛtiḥ vītā gatā āvṛtiryeṣāṃ te tānsamavalokya samudvīkṣya ||
children.translated_text: Having looked upon living beings, creatures, as uncovered: an āvṛti is a covering; those whose covering has gone are 'devoid of covering.' Having fully beheld them.
After the prior darkness has slipped away and fallen.
Of what kind?

children.text: uttarīyasyeva tviḍ yasya taduttarīyatviṭ tasminnaṃśukanibhe timire ||
children.translated_text: In darkness resembling a cloth, whose shine is like an upper garment.
Like what?
Like threads.
Like threads, that is strands, those rays.

children.text: yathā kaścit tantuvāyo 'tanupaṭān vitanute prāṇabhṛto vigatavāsaso dṛṣṭvā ||
children.translated_text: Just as some weaver stretches out broad cloths when he sees living beings without garments.

children.text: te sāndrībhūya ghanatāṃ prāpyāmbaraṃ vāso'malaṃ vimalamutpādayanti evaṃ marīcayo'pi sāndrībhūya sadyastatkṣaṇamambaramākāśaṃ śaśvatsarvadā vimalam utpādayanti ||
children.translated_text: Having become dense and reached thickness, they produce an immaculate garment, a pure sky; in the same way the rays too, having become dense, at once, in that very instant, always make the sky pure.
Of what kind?
"Broad with rows of the ten directions made clear in order."

children.text: krameṇa paryāyeṇa viśadāḥ paripāṭyā spaṣṭā daśa ca tā āśāśca daśāśā daśa diśaḥ kramaviśadāśca tā daśāśāśca tā eva daśās tāsām ālī paṅktistayā viśālaṃ vistīrṇam ||
children.translated_text: In sequence, in order, the ten directions are clear, distinct in arrangement; those ten directions themselves are the rows, and by their line it is broad, extended.
That garment too is broad with rows of ten.

children.text: tīvrabhānorgabhastyudgamaḥ kiraṇodayo vo yuṣmākamanabhimatanude anabhimatamanabhīṣṭaṃ pāpaṃ śatrurvā tasya nodanaṃ nut tasyai stādbhavatāt ||
children.translated_text: May the rising of the beams, the arising of the rays, of the intensely shining Sun be for the removal of what is unwanted by you; may it be for the driving away of the unwanted, undesired thing, whether sin or an enemy.
Like what?
As if, first of all, an emergence had been produced by fire.
Emerging is "emergence."
As if a welcome had been made.
By what sort of fire?

children.text: bhāsvadgrāvodgatena bhāsvato grāvāṇo bhāsvadgrāvāṇo'rkopalāḥ sūryakāntābhidhānā maṇiviśeṣāstebhya udgato bhāsvadgrāvodgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: By one arisen from shining stones: shining stones are sun-stones, particular jewels called <s>sūryakānta</s>; arisen from them is "arisen from shining stones."
For these, when touched by the Sun's rays, emit fire.
In the word "herbs," the brilliance located in the herbs is meant.
Because of its being situated there.
As in the expressions, "the mountain burns" and "the roads are robbed."
Obscuring it, overpowering it.
The lord of the herbs is the Moon.

children.text: tasminnoṣadhīnāṃ bhartarīndau muṣitaruci muṣitā rugyasya sa tasminmuṣitaruci hatabhāsi śuceva śokeneva proṣitābhāḥ proṣitā ābhā yāsāmoṣadhīnāṃ tāstathoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the lord of the herbs, the Moon, has had his radiance stolen, that is, when his light is destroyed, the herbs are as though bereft of brilliance through grief; they are called those whose radiance has departed.

children.text: bhartari hatatejasi patnyaḥ śokena gatadhṛtayo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: When their husband has lost his splendor, wives become deprived of firmness through grief.
In the morning, displaying, making manifest, the stones, the rocks, of the mountain called the rising mountain.
As if of what kind?
As if streaming with blood from wounds caused by the cutting of wings.

children.text: pakṣāṇāṃ chedaḥ pakṣacchedastena vraṇāsteṣāmasṛgrudhiraṃ pakṣacchedavraṇāsṛk tatsravantīti tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The cutting of wings is "wing-cutting"; from that come wounds, and their blood is "blood from wing-cutting wounds"; those which stream with it are so called.
Like limbs streaming with blood from wounds.

children.text: yato gabhastyudgama ātāmro lohito 'tastadanurañjitāḥ śilā evamutprekṣyante ||
children.translated_text: Because the rising of the rays is copper-red, red, the stones colored by that are imagined in this way.

children.text: pūrvaṃ kila parvatāḥ pakṣavanto 'bhūvaṃsteṣām indras tāṃściccheda ||
children.translated_text: Formerly, indeed, mountains had wings, and <s>Indra</s> cut them off.

children.text: gharmāṃśorādityasya ghṛṇayo mayūkhā vo yuṣmākamaṃhovighātaṃ pāpāpanodaṃ vidadhatu kurvantu ||
children.translated_text: May the beams, the rays, of the hot-rayed one, the Sun, bring about for you the destruction of distress, the removal of sin.
Quickly, in that very instant.
What are they distinguished by?
They have received an offering of argha; an argha has been given and presented to them.
By whom?
By hosts of siddhas: siddhas are those possessed of powers such as minuteness; by their groups, their multitudes.
What sort of hot-rayed one is he?
He who again, once more, puts together, makes whole.
Whom?
Those whose noses, feet, and hands have decayed.
Ghrāṇa means nose.
Aṅghrī means the two feet.
Pāṇī means the two hands.

children.text: ghrāṇaṃ cāṅghrī ca pāṇī ceti samāhāradvaṃdvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Nose, feet, and hands" is a collective copulative compound.

children.text: śīrṇā ghrāṇāṅghripāṇayo yeṣāṃ sāmarthyādaṅgināṃ te tathoktān ||
children.translated_text: Those whose noses, feet, and hands have decayed; by implication, embodied beings whose limbs are so described.
Likewise, those marked by wounded limbs with wasted members.
Those whose sounds are rattling and indistinct: a rattling, broken, unclear, inarticulate sound or noise is theirs.

children.text: ghrāṇādiluptatāyāṃ kaṇṭhauṣṭhādivraṇitāyāṃ ca kāraṇamupavarṇayannāha aghaughaiḥ pāpasamūhair dīrghāghrātāṃścirataragrastān ||
children.translated_text: Stating the cause for the loss of noses and the wounding of throats, lips, and so on, he says: by masses of sins, long smelled, or long seized.
Doing what?
Restoring to health, making free from disease.
Alone, without assistance.

children.text: rudrādayo'pi sūryamūrtim ārūḍhā eva nīrogaṃ kurvantīti saṃbandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The connection is that even <s>Rudra</s> and the others make one free from disease only when they have mounted the form of the Sun.
Of what sort of Sun?
"Whose activity is unhindered, governed by dense compassion doubled within."

children.text: antarmadhye cetasi dviguṇā ghanā bahulā ghṛṇā dayā ||
children.translated_text: Within, in the middle, in the mind, there is doubled, dense, abundant ghṛṇā, compassion.
It is both dense and compassion; thus "dense compassion."

children.text: antardviguṇā cāsau ghanaghṛṇā ca tayā nighnā paravaśā nirvighnā antarāyarahitā vṛttiryasya sa tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He whose activity is governed, dependent upon, that dense compassion doubled within, and is free from obstacles, is so called.

children.text: hāridaśvāḥ sūryasaṃbandhino 'ṃśavo raśmayo vo yuṣmākaṃ kṛcchrāṇi duḥkhāni harantvapanayantu ||
children.translated_text: May the rays belonging to the Sun, whose horses are tawny, remove and take away your hardships and sufferings.
They are further qualified as "mocking <s>Hari</s> by the play of their height."

children.text: ucchrāya uccaistvaṃ tasya yā helā līlā tayā upahasito viḍambitas tvatto'dhiko deśo'smāditi hasito harirviṣṇur yaiste ||
children.translated_text: Height is loftiness; through the play of that height, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is mocked, derided, as though laughed at with the thought, "there is a region higher than you."
The intended meaning is that they are like <s>Viṣṇu</s> after he had begun his stride.
Doing what?
Bearing, holding.
What?
Dwarfhood, shortness.
At first, in the beginning.

children.text: athānantaraṃ prāṃśavo dīrghāstathaiva yathā bhagavānnārāyaṇaḥ prathamaṃ vikramakāle vāmanatvaṃ kṛtvā prāṃśurdīrghaḥ saṃjātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, immediately afterward, they are tall and long, just as the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, at the time of his stride, first assumed dwarfhood and then became tall and long.
Again, of what kind?
They have traversed the spaces of the sky.

children.text: krāntaṃ vyāptam ākāśāntarālam ambaramadhyaṃ yaiste tathoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those by whom the inner space of the sky, the middle of the atmosphere, has been traversed or pervaded are so called.

children.text: tadanu anantaraṃ ca daśa diśo daśāśāḥ pūrayantaḥ pūrṇāḥ kurvantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that, immediately, filling the ten directions, making the ten quarters full.

children.text: tato'pi punar api viśvaṃ jagadaśnuvānā vyāpnuvantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And after that again, reaching, pervading, the whole world.
Quickly, swiftly.
Having done what?
Having cut off, drawn away, and taken away.
From what?
From darkness, from obscurity.
As from what?
As from the enemy of the gods, as from the foe of the gods.
From <s>Bali</s>, that is, from the one named <s>Bali</s>; elsewhere, from the strong one.
After both words ending in the fifth case, there is the affix tas.
This is to be connected with <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
He too, having become <s>Vāmana</s>, became tall.
And thereafter he traversed the space within the sky.
Then, after seizing the universe from <s>Bali</s>, he filled the ten directions and pervaded it.

children.text: te mayūkhā raśmayaḥ kharāṃśoḥ savituḥ saṃbandhino vo yuṣmabhyaṃ sukhaṃ śarma diśantu dadatu ||
children.translated_text: May those beams, the rays belonging to the hot-rayed sun, to <s>Savitṛ</s>, grant and give you happiness and welfare.

children.text: ye'ruṇasya sāratheraruṇatvaṃ lohitatvaṃ bahulaṃ ghanaṃ vidadhati kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: They make abundant and dense the redness, the ruddy color, of <s>Aruṇa</s>, the charioteer.
By what?
By redness, by ruddy color.
Intense, powerful.
On the mouths of the chariot-horses, on the faces of the carriage-steeds, they have the appearance of blood from wounds caused by the bit, the hue of blood from a mouth-wound.
When the head has risen, when there is an upward tossing of the head.

children.text: ye śailānāṃ parvatānāṃ śekharatvaṃ mukuṭatvaṃ tanvate vistārayanti ||
children.translated_text: They extend the condition of being crests, the condition of being crowns, for mountains.
Of what kind are they?
Abiding on mountain peaks, being those that have resorted to the summit-parts of mountains.
Or, they are those whose crests are the mountain-peaks that they have reached.
What are they doing?
Moving, going.
Where?
In the sky, in the firmament.
Making the face of day distinct, making clear the beginning of the day.

children.text: dīptāṃśor ādityasya saṃbandhinyo gāvo dīdhitayo vo yuṣmākaṃ prītiṃ sukhamutpādayantu janayantu ||
children.translated_text: May the cows, that is, the rays, belonging to the bright-rayed sun, the sun, produce and generate joy and happiness for you.
Of what kind are they?
Giving delight: those by whom delight has been given, bestowed.
For whom?
For creatures, for people.
By means of what?
By waters.
Drawn forth and released at the proper time: the proper, suitable time is the time at which they are drawn forth and emitted.

children.text: bhūyo'pi viśeṣyante pūrvāhṇe viprakīrṇāḥ ahnaḥ pūrvo bhāgastatra vikṣiptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are further qualified as scattered in the forenoon, cast forth in the earlier part of the day.
Where?
In every direction, in all directions.
When the day ceases, when it passes, at the time of sunset, they take part in withdrawal, they resort to contraction.
Again, of what kind are they?
Boats for crossing the ocean of fear of existence, which arises from long suffering.

children.text: dīrghaṃ ca tadduḥkhaṃ ca tasya prabhava utpattisthānaṃ sa cāsau bhavaśca saṃsārastasmād bhayaṃ tad evodanvān samudras tasmād uttāras tatra nāvo yānapātrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Long suffering is its source, its place of arising; that is existence, saṃsāra, and the fear from that is itself an ocean; for the crossing of that ocean they are boats, vessels of passage.
The highest, the most excellent, among purifiers and fires.
What kind of joy?
Immeasurable, without limit.
The word gāvaḥ is a pun and is undivided in form.
For gāvaḥ also means cows.

children.text: tā api payobhirdugdhaiḥ samucitasamayākṛṣṭasṛṣṭaiḥ prajānāṃ dattānandā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those cows too, by their fluids, that is, their milk, drawn forth and released at the proper time, become givers of delight to creatures.
In the forenoon, at dawn, they become scattered.
At the end of the day they take part in being gathered in.
And, truly given, they are immediately boats for crossing the ocean of fear of existence arising from long suffering.
Those who know the tradition say that by their fluids, through the satisfaction of brahmins and sacred fires, people cross saṃsāra.

children.text: dinakarakiraṇā ravipādā bhavatāṃ kalmaṣasya pāpasya ketavo vināśakāḥ kalpantāṃ saṃpadyantām ||
children.translated_text: May the rays of the maker of day, the feet of the sun, become destroyers of your stain, of sin.
Without doubt, certainly.
This is an adverbial qualifier of the action.

children.text: svaṃ ca cittaṃ ca svacittaṃ tasya prathitā pṛthutarā pṛthvī sā cāsau prārthanā ca tasyāḥ kalpavṛkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: One's own mind is svacitta; for its renowned, very broad and great prayer, they are wish-fulfilling trees.

children.text: ye lokānāṃ prajānāṃ prabodhaṃ tattvajñānaṃ vidadhati kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: They produce awakening, knowledge of reality, among people and creatures.
Bondage is threefold: natural, derivative, and in the form of a dakṣiṇā-sā.

children.text: tena hi baddhā dehino na mucyante ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, embodied beings bound by it are not released.
For the destruction, the removal, of that bondage, they are the single cause, the chief cause.
Of what kind of creatures?

children.text: śirasi mastake natirnamaskārastatra rasastenābaddho viracitaḥ saṃdhyāñjaliryaiste tathoktāsteṣām ||
children.translated_text: Of those for whom, on the head, in bowing and reverence, a twilight handful-offering has been formed, bound together by devotion.
Like what?
Like the expectation of a broad mass of lotuses.
A broad mass of lotuses is an extensive lotus-bed.
Or, broad and also a mass of lotuses; like the expectation of that.
Being the sole cause of the destruction of bondage is also being the sole cause of the removal of the bud-state.
Prabodha means knowledge and also blossoming.
May the rays of the fierce-shining sun protect you and save you from stain, from sin.
Pleasant at the face of the day: causing happiness at the beginning of the day.
This is a statement of their own nature.

children.text: punarapi ca nirūpyante rāyo dravyasya dhārāḥ prapātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And again they are described: streams and cascades of wealth.
Where?
In distress over wealth, in bodily suffering caused by the need for possessions.

children.text: dhanāyā dhanecchā tasyā āpatprārthanā dhanasya prāptistatrāpi ||
children.translated_text: Or, dhanāyā is the desire for wealth; its calamity is the request, and also the obtaining, of wealth.
Immediately, at that very moment.
They are handholds: the meaning is that they lift one up by taking one in their hands.
Where?
At the precipice, in hell, in misfortune.

children.text: tattvālokaikadīpāḥ tattvasya paramārthasyāloke darśane ekadīpāḥ prakāśakatvāt ||
children.translated_text: They are the single lamps for the sight of truth, for the vision of ultimate reality, because they illuminate it.

children.text: tridaśapatirindrastasya puraṃ nagaram amarāvatī tatra prasthitiḥ prasthānaṃ tatra vīthya eva panthāna eva ||
children.translated_text: The lord of the thirty gods is <s>Indra</s>; his city is <s>Amarāvatī</s>; for setting out toward that city, the streets themselves are the paths.
Again, what are they like?

children.text: nirvāṇodyogino mokṣotsukāste ca te yoginaśca teṣāṃ pragamo'punarāvṛttistasya nijā ātmīyā sā cāsau tanuśca tasyā dvārdvāraṃ tasyāṃ vetrāyamāṇāḥ pratīhārā ivācarantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who are intent on nirvāṇa, eager for liberation, are yogins; their progress is non-return. Their own, personal body is the doorway of that progress, and in that doorway they act like doorkeepers wielding staffs.

children.text: ye hi siddhā yogino bhavanti te hi sūryatanudvāreṇa na skhalanamāsādayanti ||
children.translated_text: For those who are perfected yogins do not meet with a stumble through the doorway of the sun's body.

children.text: udyuktānāṃ yogināṃ tu sūryatanurdvāḥ tatra dvāḥsthāḥ prayātuṃ na dadati ||
children.translated_text: But for yogins who are merely striving, the sun's body is the doorway; there the door-guards do not allow them to pass.
Or else, because one goes forward by means of it, it is called pragama, a path.
The compound means: the progress of yogins intent on nirvāṇa, and the doorway of their own body.

children.text: caṇḍarocīruco gharmaghṛṇipādāścintitānāṃ manorathānāmucitaṃ yogyaṃ vo yuṣmākaṃ ceṣṭantāṃ vyāpriyantāṃ saṃpādayantu vā ||
children.translated_text: May the rays of the hot-rayed one, the feet of the heat-rayed sun, busy themselves with what is suitable for your desired wishes, or accomplish them.
What are they doing?
They are performing, carrying out.
What is that?
The state of being a beautiful crest-jewel, that is, the state of being a lovely summit-gem.
Where?
On the immovable one, the mountain.
Of what kind?
Eastern, belonging to the eastern direction.
Prāk means first.
Anaticiram means for a short time.
Of what kind are they?
As if releasing rocanā-water, that is, yellow pigment-water.
Pracuram means abundant.
For the adorning of the directions, the quarters.
The dative case is used in the sense of purpose.
Uccakaiḥ means exceedingly.
At first, because of their extreme redness, the rays of the fierce-rayed sun are imagined as a jewel on the head.
After that, when they have become tawny, they are imagined as rocanā-water.
Again, of what kind are they?
They are worshipped, looked upon with longing.
By whom?
By the edges of the eyes, the corners of the eyes, of those called cakras.
Avicalaiḥ means unmoving.
How?
In such a way as to be clever, artful.
By those eager for flattering words, desirous of coaxing.

children.text: cakravākāṇāṃ hi bhagavati gabhastimālinyabhyudite sati viyuktānāṃ parasparaṃ samāgamo bhavatīti sādaraṃ tadruco'rcyanta ityevamabhihitam ||
children.translated_text: For when the blessed <s>Gabhastimālin</s>, the sun, has risen, cakravāka birds who have been separated are reunited with one another; therefore his rays are reverently worshipped. This is what has been stated.
Acaramāḥ means not western.

children.text: bhānoḥ saṃbandhīni dīdhitīnāṃ daśa śatāni sahasramiti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: The ten hundreds of rays belonging to <s>Bhānu</s> amount to a thousand.

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ śivaṃ bhadraṃ dadhatu puṣṇantu kurvantu vā ||
children.translated_text: May they bear, nourish, or make auspiciousness and welfare for you.
This is because verbal roots have many meanings.

children.text: kiṃbhūtānītyāha yāni ekaṃ jyotirekaṃ tejaḥ pradhānamālokakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: He states what kind they are: they are said to be one light, one radiance, the chief cause of illumination.
Again, of what sort are they?
They are two sights, two eyes.
In the three worlds, in the triple universe, they are spoken of.
By whom?
By lotus-born mouths, that is, by the mouths of <s>Brahmā</s>.
How many?
Four, furnished with the number four.
They are the fifth among the elements beginning with earth.

children.text: pañcānāṃ bhūtānāṃ tejasi sati pañca saṃkhyā sampadyate ||
children.translated_text: When fire is present among the five elements, the number five is completed.

children.text: tathā ṛtuṣu vasantādiṣu ṣaṭsvalam atyarthaṃ nānāvidhānyuccāvacaprakārāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, among the six seasons beginning with spring, they are exceedingly manifold, of many different high and low kinds.
Because they are differentiated by distinctions such as intense and mild.
Again, what kind are they?

children.text: saptatridaśamuninutāni tridaśamunayo devarṣayo'triprabhṛtayaḥ sapta ca te tridaśamunayaśca tairnutāni ||
children.translated_text: They are praised by seven divine sages: the divine sages, beginning with <s>Atri</s>, are seven, and they are divine sages; by them they are praised.
Again, of what kind are they?
They partake of the eight directions, resting in the eight quarters.

children.text: pūrvāhṇe dinamukhe navatvaṃ pratyagratvaṃ yānti bhajante ||
children.translated_text: In the forenoon, at the face of the day, they attain newness, freshness.
First, they have oneness as light.
Then they have twoness as sight.
They have threeness as worlds.
They have the number four in the four faces of <s>Brahmā</s>.
They are fivefold in the form of earth and the other elements.
They have sixness through the number of spring and the other seasons.
They have sevenness through <s>Atri</s> and the others.
They have manyness through distinctions such as intense and mild.
They have eightness through their sharing in the eight directions.
Difference arises from difference of substratum.
Because of verbal similarity, the newness in the forenoon is shown as navatva, the possession of the number nine.

children.text: mārtaṇḍasya bhānorabhīśavo dīdhitayo vo yuṣmākamaśubhabhide'kalyāṇavināśāya bhavantu jāyantām ||
children.translated_text: May the rays, the beams, of <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, <s>Bhānu</s>, arise for the destruction of your inauspiciousness.
Ciram means for a long time.
With what qualification?

children.text: ye dharitryā bhuvo rasaṃ jalaṃ dhayanti pibanti ||
children.translated_text: They drink the rasa, the water, of the earth.
Asakṛt means many times.
Like what do they drink?
As if drying, as if endowed with drying power.

children.text: śoṣiṇo'pi śramamiva dadhataḥ khedamiva dadhānā bibhrāṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though drying, they are as if bearing fatigue, carrying weariness.
He gives the reason for the assumption of fatigue: their universe is wearied by repeated movement.

children.text: āvṛttyā paunaḥpunyena bhrāntaṃ paryaṭitaṃ viśvaṃ jagadyaiste tathoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are so called because the whole world has been roamed over, traversed, by them again and again.
Where?
In summer, the hot season.
They are drying by their own heat.

children.text: punarutprekṣate dāvāgnitaptā iva jalam atīva narā dhayanti tadvadete ityutprekṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again he imagines: as people scorched by a forest fire drink water excessively, so too these rays are imagined to do.
Those rays, in the rainy season, are udvāntatoyāḥ, having vomited forth water, having poured out water.
Of what kind?

children.text: āttapānātiśayaruja iva āttā prāptā pānātiśayarug yaiste ||
children.translated_text: As if afflicted by excessive drinking: they are those by whom pain from excessive drinking has been obtained.
In the cold season, in winter, they are not fierce, but gentle and weak.

children.text: yathā ko'pi pānīyapānātiśayāt prāptavedano mando bhavati tadvadete'pi ||
children.translated_text: Just as someone becomes sluggish from pain caused by excessive drinking of water, so these too become mild.

children.text: bhāsāṃ dīdhitīnāṃ daśaśatī gharmatviṣaḥ sūryasaṃbandhinī vo yuṣmabhyaṃ śarma sukhaṃ kalyāṇaṃ diśatu yacchatu ||
children.translated_text: May the ten-hundredfold host of rays, the beams belonging to the hot-rayed sun, grant you comfort, happiness, and welfare.
Like what?
Like a row of beard-hairs, like a line of hair on the face.
What is it doing?
Somewhat emerging, rising up.
Where?
At the face of the day, at dawn.
Elsewhere, it emerges on the face of young men.
What is it doing?
It is extending, spreading out.
What?
A condition, a state.
Of whom?
Of the brides who are the directions.
The directions themselves are brides; of them.
Of what kind?
Lovely through an exceedingly sweet light.

children.text: samadhikaḥ samyag adhiko madhuro mṛdurya ālokaḥ prakāśastena ramyām ||
children.translated_text: Samadhika means properly abundant; through a sweet, soft āloka, that is, radiance, it is lovely.
Again, of what sort is it?
It has a tawny color brought out by a slight attainment of maturity.

children.text: prauḍhiḥ prauḍhatvaṃ tasyā leśaḥ ārūḍhaścāsau prauḍhileśaśceti samāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Prauḍhi is maturity; a leśa, a trace, of that. 'It has mounted, and it is a trace of maturity': this is the compound ārūḍha-prauḍhi-leśa.

children.text: tenotkalito vardhitaḥ kapilimā kapilatvaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā ||
children.translated_text: By that, kapilimā, tawny coloring, has been heightened; it is so called because that belongs to it.
Alaṃkṛti means ornament, adornment.
Kevalā eva means only, alone.
At the face of the day of what kind?
Where the splendor of lotus-like eyes is expanding; it is so described, and there.
All this must also be connected with the row of beard-hairs.
That too spreads over the brides a condition lovely through exceedingly sweet beauty.
It has tawny coloring brought out by a slight attainment of maturity.

children.text: alaṃkṛtiścāsau kevalaiva mukhasya sampadyata ityādi samānam ||
children.translated_text: And that alone becomes the ornament of the face; the rest is the same.

children.text: timirariporādityasya sa tviṣāṃ bhāsāmudgama udayastrāṇāya rakṣāyai vo yuṣmākaṃ stādbhavatāt ||
children.translated_text: May that rising, the emergence, of the lights, the radiances, of the enemy of darkness, namely <s>Āditya</s>, be for your protection and preservation.
Even though slight, even though very slender.
Of what sort?
One that was praised.
By whom?
By the bull-marked one, the bearer of the bow <s>Pināka</s>.
As if by one who was afraid.
Thinking what?

children.text: maulīndor maulicandrasyaiṣo 'yaṃ dyutiṃ prabhāṃ mā moṣīnmā khaṇḍayatviti ||
children.translated_text: 'May this not steal, may it not impair, the splendor, the radiance, of the moon on my crest.'

children.text: dhātrā brahmaṇā ca yaḥ stuta iti saṃbandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: and it was praised by <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>.
Praised as being of what sort?
Beginning with pratyagra.
As if seated happily in the hollow of a lotus that had just then blossomed.
As if saying, 'May it not bring about some painful condition of contraction.'
Likewise by dark <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as if he were by nature afraid of the humiliation of his own dark body by the darkness.
Alam means exceedingly.
The word iva everywhere indicates poetic supposition.
As if saying, 'Surely, mistaking me for darkness, it may overpower my own body.'

children.text: ādyairapi devaiḥ stuta iti mahattvaṃ raverdarśayati ||
children.translated_text: By saying that it was praised even by the chief gods, he shows the greatness of the sun.

children.text: te sahasratviṣaḥ sahasraraśmerusrā gabhastayo'nabhimataṃ duḥkhaṃ visraṃsayantu dhvaṃsayantu ||
children.translated_text: May those usrāḥ, rays or beams, of the thousand-rayed one destroy and shatter what is undesired, that is, suffering.
Vo means of you, your.
Drutam means quickly, swiftly.
By which the lotus-bed, and the world, is made to breathe at dawn, in the morning.
After destroying.
What?
Tamisrā, darkness, or night.
Doing what?

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ pṛthulaṃ vyoma gaganam dīrghā āyatā daśa diśo daśāśāḥ sapadi tatkṣaṇaṃ vyastavelāmbhaso'bdhīn vikṣiptavelājalān samudrān kurvadbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Making the wide, broad vyoman, the sky, and the long, extended ten directions, the ten quarters, immediately, at that very moment, and making the oceans have their shore-waters scattered.
And making the earth, the ground.
Of what sort?
Broad with the visible expanse of various mountains, cities, and trees.

children.text: nagāḥ parvatāḥ nagarāṇi pattanāni nagā vṛkṣāste ca te nānāprakārāśceti samāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nagāḥ are mountains; nagarāṇi are towns; nagāḥ are trees. These are of many kinds: such is the compound.
Dṛśyā means visible, perceptible.

children.text: dṛśyāśca te nānānaganagaranagās teṣām ābhogo vistārastena pṛthvīṃ vistīrṇām ||
children.translated_text: They are visible and are various mountains, cities, and trees; by their ābhoga, their expanse, the earth is broad.
